"Good morning, Karthik. My name is Dr. Lee. What brings you in today?"

"Hi, Dr. Lee. Karthik has had a really sore throat for the past three days. He's also been running a fever."

"Okay, Karthik, can you point to where it hurts?"

*Karthik points to his throat.*

"And how severe would you say the pain is on a scale of 1 to 10, with 10 being the worst?"

"It's about a 7, doctor. It really hurts when I swallow."

"I see. And regarding the fever, Mrs. Reddy, what has been the highest temperature you've recorded?"

"It was 39 degrees Celsius last night. We've been giving him acetaminophen, which brings it down a bit, but it goes back up."

"Any other symptoms, like a cough, runny nose, or body aches?"

"No, just the sore throat and fever. He's been a bit tired, but otherwise, no other complaints."

"Has Karthik been around anyone else who's been sick recently?"

"Not that we know of, no."

"Alright, Karthik, let's take a look. Can you open wide and say 'Ahhh' for me?"

*Upon examination, I observed erythematous and edematous tonsils with white exudates bilaterally. Palpation revealed tender anterior cervical lymphadenopathy.*

"Okay, Karthik, we're just going to do a quick swab of your throat to check for strep. It might feel a little ticklish."

*The rapid strep test was performed and returned positive.*

"Alright, Karthik, you can sit up now. We've got the results from the swab."
